what: Week Number tells you which week of the year a date belongs to. Many workplaces, schools and factories plan by week number, and the tool answers "which week is it?" in a moment.

There is more than one way to count weeks. The tool shows the ISO 8601 week (Monday start, week 1 contains the first Thursday), the Sunday-start system used in the USA, Canada and Japan, and the Saturday-start system used in parts of the Middle East.
You can also look up the dates of any week number and see a table of every week in a year, ready to copy or download.
uses: Match dates to the week numbers used in schedules, sprints and payroll.
Read delivery weeks like "week 32" in orders and factory plans.
Count teaching weeks and plan homework by week.
Check whether a colleague abroad means the same week as you.
Download the year table to use in Excel or Google Sheets.
tutorial: The tool starts with today. Choose any other date, or use Week before and Week after.
ISO 8601 is the default in most countries; the Sunday-start system is chosen in the US and Canada. Your choice is remembered.
The big number is the week. Underneath you see the full date, and for ISO the standard code such as 2026-W48-1.
The boxes show when the week starts and ends, how many weeks the year has, the day of the year and the days left.
The table shows the same date in all three systems; your chosen one is highlighted.
Type a year and a week number under "Find the dates of a week".
Pick a year to list all its weeks. Press Copy table or Download CSV.
features: ISO 8601, Sunday start and Saturday start.
Start and end of the week for any date.
Days that belong to the previous or next year are explained.
Dates of any week number in any year.
All weeks of a year, with copy and CSV download.
Dates are written the way your device shows them.

example.title: Worked example: a delivery in week 2
example.text: A supplier in Germany promises delivery in "KW 2" of 2027. Sam in the USA types 2027 and 2 under "Find the dates of a week" with ISO 8601 selected and sees Mon 11 Jan – Sun 17 Jan 2027. Switching to Sunday start shows his own calendar’s week 2 is 3–9 January, a week earlier, so he notes the ISO dates.

tips: When someone gives you a week number, ask which system they use, or assume ISO if they are in Europe.
The ISO code like 2026-W48-1 is handy in file names and spreadsheets.
Use Week after to step through a planning period quickly.
A CSV download opens directly in most spreadsheet apps.
problems: My calendar shows a different week number
Your calendar probably uses another system. Switch the week system to match.
That is correct in the ISO system when 1 January falls on a Friday, Saturday or Sunday.
